intro_en: In this lesson you will use the て-form to say several actions in one sentence. You say them in order, like "I get up, brush my teeth, and eat". You will also join adjectives with くて / で. You will learn to say "after doing" with てから / あとで. You will ask "how?" with どうやって. You will also say how someone looks, like "he has big eyes". At the end, you can explain everyday steps in Japanese. For example, how to change trains or put money in at an ATM.

g16-1.explanation_en: You can say several actions in one sentence, in the order they happen. Put the earlier verbs in the て-form. Only the last verb ends with ます / ました / てください. Tamil works the same way. Look at "எழுந்து, பல் துலக்கி, சாப்பிடுகிறேன்" (I get up, brush my teeth, and eat). The words "எழுந்து" and "துலக்கி" show no time (past or present). Only the last verb "சாப்பிடுகிறேன்" shows the time. The Japanese て-form is the same. Present or past shows only on the last verb. Say the actions in the order they happened. Usually you join only two or three て-forms in one sentence.
g16-1.tamil_parallel_en: Japanese て works like the Tamil ending -து / -இ: எழுந்து, பல் துலக்கி, சாப்பிடுகிறேன் ("having got up, having brushed my teeth, I eat") = 起きて、歯を磨いて、食べます. In both languages, only the last verb shows the time (past or present).
g16-1.formation_en: V1 て-form + 、+ V2 て-form + 、+ V3 ます / ました / てください (only the last verb shows the time)
g16-1.pitfalls_en: The て-form shows no time. So don’t put every verb in the past, like "ました、ました". The last verb is enough. Don’t use て to give a reason for another action. For a reason, use から (Lesson 9).

g16-2.explanation_en: You can give two qualities of one thing in one sentence. Put the first adjective (describing word) in its joining form. For an い-adjective, drop the last い and add くて (大きい → 大きくて). Only いい is different: it becomes よくて. For a な-adjective or a noun, add で (静か → 静かで、学生 → 学生で). This is like adding "-ஆகவும்" in Tamil. For example, "இந்த அறை வெளிச்சமாகவும் சுத்தமாகவும் இருக்கிறது" (this room is bright and clean). Both qualities must go the same way. Both are good, or both are bad. Sometimes they go opposite ways, like "small but comfortable". Then don’t use くて. Use が (but).
g16-2.tamil_parallel_en: Like Tamil "-ஆகவும் ... -ஆகவும்": இந்த அறை வெளிச்சமாகவும் சுத்தமாகவும் இருக்கிறது ("this room is bright and clean") = この部屋は明るくて、きれいです.
g16-2.formation_en: い-adj: 〜い → 〜くて (大きい → 大きくて、いい → よくて) / な-adj: 〜 + で (静か → 静かで) / N: N + で (学生 → 学生で、日本人 → 日本人で)
g16-2.pitfalls_en: Don’t add で to an い-adjective: ×明るいで → ○明るくて. For いい, it is not ×いくて. It is ○よくて. Sometimes two ideas go opposite ways. For example, "that shop is cheap, but the food isn’t tasty". Then don’t use くて. Use が.

g16-3.explanation_en: Add から after the て-form of the first verb. It means "V2 happens only after V1 is finished". Plain て only gives the order. てから says more strongly: first finish this, then do the next thing. It is like Tamil "சாப்பிட்டு விட்டுப் போகிறேன்" (I’ll eat and then go). It is also like "வீட்டுப்பாடம் செய்து முடித்த பிறகு விளையாடுவேன்" (I’ll play after finishing my homework). Here too, only the last verb shows the time (past or present). Usually you use てから only once in a sentence.
g16-3.tamil_parallel_en: Like Tamil "செய்து முடித்த பிறகு" (after finishing doing): வீட்டுப்பாடம் செய்து முடித்த பிறகு விளையாடுவேன் ("I’ll play after I finish my homework") = 宿題をしてから、遊びます.
g16-3.formation_en: V1 て-form + から、+ V2 (ます / ました / てください)
g16-3.pitfalls_en: Don’t mix up these two. 食べますから is ます + から. It means "because" (a reason). 食べてから is て + から. It means "after". For "after", the verb before から is always in the て-form.

g16-4.explanation_en: To say "after ...", use あとで. After a noun, add の. For example, ご飯のあとで (after the meal) and 仕事のあとで (after work). After a verb, you need the た-form (た形). You will learn it fully in Lesson 19. For now, here is a simple rule. Take the て-form. Change て → た and で → だ. Now you have the た-form (見て → 見た、読んで → 読んだ、して → した). Tamil does the same thing. "பார்த்த பிறகு" (after seeing) is the past form "பார்த்த" + "பிறகு". Japanese says 見た + あとで. あとで is looser than てから. It can also mean "sometime later".
g16-4.tamil_parallel_en: Tamil uses a past form + பிறகு. Japanese uses the た-form + あとで: சாப்பாட்டுக்குப் பிறகு ("after the meal") = ご飯のあとで ; படம் பார்த்த பிறகு ("after watching the film") = 映画を見たあとで.
g16-4.formation_en: N + の + あとで、〜 / V た-form (て→た: 見て→見た、飲んで→飲んだ、行って→行った、して→した、来て→来た) + あとで、〜
g16-4.pitfalls_en: Don’t forget の after a noun: ×ご飯あとで → ○ご飯のあとで. Don’t use the ます-form of the verb: ×見ますあとで → ○見たあとで.

g16-5.explanation_en: You can talk about one part of a person or a place. Put the whole person with は. は marks the topic (what you are talking about). Put the part with が. Then add the adjective. 田中さんは目が大きいです = about Tanaka-san: her eyes are big. It is like Tamil "அவருக்குக் கண் பெரிது" (he has big eyes). It is also like "அண்ணனுக்கு உயரம் அதிகம்" (my elder brother is tall). In Tamil, the person takes "-க்கு" and the part is the main word. You can also say 田中さんの目は大きいです. But then you are talking about the eyes. With は〜が, you are talking about the person. It works for places too. For example, チェンナイは人が多いです (Chennai has a lot of people).
g16-5.tamil_parallel_en: Like Tamil "person-க்கு + part + adjective": அண்ணனுக்கு உயரம் அதிகம் ("my elder brother is tall", word for word "to elder brother, height is a lot") = 兄は背が高いです.
g16-5.formation_en: N1 (person / place: the whole) + は + N2 (part / feature) + が + adj です
g16-5.pitfalls_en: For height, use 背が高い / 背が低い. Don’t say ×背が長い or ×背が短い. The part takes が. Don’t say ×目を大きい. Don’t put two は in one sentence, like ×目は大きい.

g16-6.explanation_en: どうやって is a question word. It asks for the way to do something: "how, in what way". Use it for questions like "How do I get to the station?" or "How do I use this machine?". The answer often has "N で" (the road or the tool). Or it has a て-form chain (V1て、V2ます). Keep these three apart. どう (how is it? Lesson 8) asks about how something is. どうして (why? Lesson 9) asks for a reason. どうやって asks for the way to do it. It comes before the verb. Usually it comes after the place or the thing.
g16-6.tamil_parallel_en: Like Tamil "எப்படி" when you ask the way to do something: ஸ்டேஷனுக்கு எப்படிப் போவது? ("How do I get to the station?") = 駅までどうやって行きますか.
g16-6.formation_en: (N まで / N を) + どうやって + V ますか → Answer: N で V ます / V1 て、V2 ます
g16-6.pitfalls_en: どうやって means "how to do it". どうして means "why". They sound alike, so Tamil learners often mix them up. どうですか (how is it?) is different again. It asks how something is.

g16-7.explanation_en: You can end a sentence with 。 and start the next one with そして or それから. This links the two sentences. そして = "and / and then". It adds actions or qualities (この町は静かです。そして、きれいです。). それから = "after that". It gives the order of actions. You also use it to add "and one more thing" to a list. It is like starting a new Tamil sentence with "அப்புறம்", "பிறகு" or "அதன் பிறகு". Sometimes a 〜て、〜て chain gets long. Then it sounds natural to end the sentence. Go on with そして / それから.
g16-7.tamil_parallel_en: Like starting a new Tamil sentence with "அதன் பிறகு" (after that): வங்கிக்குப் போகிறேன். அதன் பிறகு தபால் நிலையத்துக்குப் போகிறேன் ("I’ll go to the bank. After that I’ll go to the post office.") = 銀行へ行きます。それから、郵便局へ行きます.
g16-7.formation_en: Sentence 1。+ そして / それから、+ Sentence 2。
g16-7.pitfalls_en: そして / それから come at the start of a sentence. Don’t put them in the middle, like いきますそして. どうして (why) is a different word.

items.L16-q01: 押す = おす (அழுத்த, to press). Its て-form is おして. おきて is 起きて (எழுந்து, getting up). That is a different verb.
items.L16-q02: 強い = つよい (வலிமையான, strong). よわい is 弱い (பலவீனமான, weak), the opposite word. There is no word つおい.
items.L16-q03: 足 = あし (கால், leg / foot). Don’t read し as じ, like あじ. はし is 箸 (சாப்ஸ்டிக், chopsticks).
items.L16-q04: め = 目 (கண், eye). 日 (ひ) and 月 (つき) look alike, but they are different words. 耳 = みみ (காது, ear).
items.L16-q05: みがく = 磨く (துலக்க, to brush / polish). 摩・麻・魔 look alike. They all have the 麻 part. For "brush", the right one is 磨. It has 石 (stone) at the bottom.
items.L16-q06: To say a person is short, use 背が低い. 短い is for length, like a pencil or a river. Don’t use it for height.
items.L16-q07: I get off the train (降りて, இறங்கி) and get on the bus. So 降りて is right. The opposite of 乗ります is 降ります. 入れる means "to put in", so it does not fit.
items.L16-q08: There is no window, so the room is dark (暗い, இருட்டு). 明るい (வெளிச்சமான, bright) is the opposite word. It does not fit the reason.
items.L16-q09: 歯を磨きます = I brush my teeth (பல் துலக்குகிறேன்). The verb for 歯 is 磨く. 押す (அழுத்த, to press) does not fit.
items.L16-q10: I put sugar in my coffee = 入れます (போடுகிறேன்). Remember the pattern "N に N を 入れる". 引く = to pull (இழுக்க), so it does not fit.
items.L16-q11: それから (அதன் பிறகு, after that) joins two actions in order. So it is right. どうして (why) and どうやって (how) are question words.
items.L16-q12: 背が高くない (not tall) = 背が低い (குட்டை, short). 足が長い (long legs) says nothing about height.
items.L16-q13: 明るくない (not bright) = 暗い (இருட்டு, dark). 汚い (அழுக்கு, dirty) is not about light.
items.L16-q14: V てから = after V is finished. 宿題のあとで means the same. 遊んでから、宿題をします turns the order around. しませんから gives a reason: "because I don’t do it".
items.L16-q15: A verb in the middle of the sentence must be in the て-form: 磨く → 磨いて (き → いて). 磨きて is a wrong form. The ます-form comes only at the end.
items.L16-q16: 静か is a な-adjective, so you join it with で. くて is only for い-adjectives (大きくて).
items.L16-q17: 安い is an い-adjective. Drop い and add くて: 安くて. Tamil learners often put で after an い-adjective, like 安いで. That is wrong.
items.L16-q18: In the "N1 は N2 が adj" pattern, が marks the part (背). 背を高い, with を, is wrong. 高い is an adjective, not a verb.
items.L16-q19: For "after doing ...", use the て-form + から: 入れてから. 入れますから would mean "because I put it in" (a reason).
items.L16-q20: Before あとで, the verb is in the た-form: 見た あとで. Don’t use the て-form, like 見て あとで. A ます-form like 見ました does not come in the middle of a sentence.
items.L16-q21: The answer バスで (by bus) gives a way of going. So the question is どうやって (எப்படி, how). どうして means "why". Its answer would end with 〜から.
items.L16-q22: 田中さんは 目が 大きくて、きれいです。 This is the "N1 は N2 が adj" pattern. The first adjective 大きい takes its joining form 大きくて. The last adjective ends with です.
items.L16-q23: 朝 起きて、シャワーの あとで 朝ご飯を 食べます。 First comes the て-form (起きて). Then "N の あとで". At the end comes を + a ます verb.
items.L16-q24: 駅で 電車に 乗って、会社へ 行きます。 The verb 乗る takes に (電車に乗る). The first action is in the て-form. The last action uses ます.
items.L16-q25: [1] and [2] are actions in the middle of the sentence. So they take the て-form (磨いて、乗って). 乗る goes with に, so 降りて does not fit there. [3] starts a new sentence. The word that links it with "after that" is それから.
